SCORE: successor_shell_budget | behavior_evidence=4 | geometry_necessity=3 | novelty=2 | downstream_mechanism=4 | falsifiability=3 | implementability=2 | exploration_value=2
SCOPE: successor_shell_budget | OUT_OF_SCOPE | It specifies train-only directed transitions and a curved child assignment coupled through successor-conditioned geodesic scoring, with SID/prefix/Stage3 outcomes. However, it does not unambiguously specify the required behavior-off, Euclidean geometry-off, and both-on comparison protocol; “beats both controls” does not define the behavior-off arm. Add those three matched arms to satisfy the scope contract.
EVIDENCE: successor_shell_budget | c36f3fe9672167fe:E1 c36f3fe9672167fe:E2 c36f3fe9672167fe:E5 c36f3fe9672167fe:E12 c36f3fe9672167fe:E13 c36f3fe9672167fe:E14 c36f3fe9672167fe:E15
OBJECTION: successor_shell_budget | The equation's positive-part difference against c_alt does not clearly define which alternative is selected or how it corresponds to the empirical successor-child distribution; moreover the proposed 32-way T1 budget can alter capacity independently of the behavior/geometry mechanism.
COUNTEREXAMPLE: successor_shell_budget | With one successor-child and all candidate child codewords coincident, d(u,c_m)=d(u,c_alt), so the geodesic separation term is zero for every assignment and supplies no behavior-geometry coupling signal.
RATIONALE: successor_shell_budget | E5 provides measured, stratified transition entropy with support; it is relevant but does not establish successor modes cluster within T1 subtrees, so 4 rather than 5. The geodesic operation is explicit (E12-E14), but a matched Euclidean transform could reproduce a distance-based preference and no curvature-specific advantage/cancellation analysis is supplied (3). No cited-work/ledger trace beyond claims in the proposal is available (novelty 2; bounded check: compare the exact equation with the cited-work and experiment ledger). The child partition → conditional predictability → beam survival chain has named diagnostics and directions (4). Controls are not sufficiently enumerated/matched (3). The multi-term quantizer/loss and candidate-alt definition need clarification for implementation, and the frozen-time estimate is only a proposal (2; bounded check: implement a one-batch shape/numerics test and benchmark).

SCORE: curved_transition_residual | behavior_evidence=4 | geometry_necessity=3 | novelty=2 | downstream_mechanism=4 | falsifiability=3 | implementability=3 | exploration_value=1
SCOPE: curved_transition_residual | OUT_OF_SCOPE | The training-only successor distribution directly shifts the residual through Lorentz transport before curved quantization, so behavior and geometry are coupled in the core path. But the proposal does not explicitly name matched behavior-off, Euclidean geometry-off, and both-on comparisons; “both controls” is not a sufficiently specified comparison set. State those arms to meet the scope contract.
EVIDENCE: curved_transition_residual | 36d2c6fd13e0d45f:E1 36d2c6fd13e0d45f:E2 36d2c6fd13e0d45f:E5 36d2c6fd13e0d45f:E12 36d2c6fd13e0d45f:E13 36d2c6fd13e0d45f:E14 36d2c6fd13e0d45f:E15 36d2c6fd13e0d45f:E16
OBJECTION: curved_transition_residual | The behavior direction is the unconditional per-item successor mean, not the continuation mode remaining after the actual prefix; subtracting it could remove item-identifying signal or average incompatible branches.
COUNTEREXAMPLE: curved_transition_residual | If two equally likely successors have tangent vectors +v and -v, then μ_i=0; transport subtracts nothing, so the advertised transition-conditioned residual effect disappears despite nonzero branching.
RATIONALE: curved_transition_residual | E5 supports heterogeneous successor predictability with measured coverage in the reported bins, but not the residual-mode premise (4). Explicit log/parallel transport/exp and geodesic assignment are given, and the Euclidean arm is referenced in E15; necessity beyond a matched Euclidean residual shift is not argued (3). The proposal itself distinguishes its operation from other steering approaches, but no traceable prior-art/ledger evidence is included (2; bounded check: equation-level ledger and cited-work comparison). The residual assignment → token predictability → beam/Recall chain is explicit with diagnostics/directions (4). Three controls and a failure threshold are mentioned generally, not fully matched and defined (3). It is nearly implementable with safeguards and cost, but the frame/anchor and decoder parameterization need exact convention/shape validation (3). Exploration value is low because tangent_successor_residual and successor-geodesic mechanisms are already measured in E6-E7 (1).

SCORE: userbranch_hyperbolic_transport | behavior_evidence=3 | geometry_necessity=3 | novelty=2 | downstream_mechanism=4 | falsifiability=3 | implementability=3 | exploration_value=2
SCOPE: userbranch_hyperbolic_transport | OUT_OF_SCOPE | It names popularity-adjusted train transitions, parent-conditioned branch aggregation, and a Mobius-transported residual used in curved child assignment. It does not explicitly lay out the required behavior-off, Euclidean geometry-off, and both-on comparisons; “both-on” and ablation language do not identify all three matched arms. Add the comparison definitions.
EVIDENCE: userbranch_hyperbolic_transport | c297abf493fe5d23:E1 c297abf493fe5d23:E2 c297abf493fe5d23:E5 c297abf493fe5d23:E12 c297abf493fe5d23:E13 c297abf493fe5d23:E14 c297abf493fe5d23:E15 c297abf493fe5d23:E16
OBJECTION: userbranch_hyperbolic_transport | The branch signal is conditioned on an already assigned parent prefix, but the specification does not make clear whether successor items have that same parent under the evolving codebooks; the grouping and conditioning can therefore be unstable or circular.
COUNTEREXAMPLE: userbranch_hyperbolic_transport | If no successor in the cached top-M set has prefix p, the specified zero fallback gives b=0; then x'=log(exp(r)⊕exp(0))=r, so the behavior-geometry pathway is exactly inactive for that item.
RATIONALE: userbranch_hyperbolic_transport | E5 is measured successor entropy, not evidence for parent-specific branches; E9 gives a related train-only profile signal but not this conditional statistic, so 3 (bounded check: measure parent-conditioned branch coverage and held-out-train profile lift). Curved Mobius transport and geodesic scoring act in assignment (E12-E14), plausibly non-Euclidean but no necessity argument against matched control (3). It is described as distinct from other steering mechanisms, yet no traceable ledger/prior-art comparison supports more than a routine variation (2). The proposed child-token predictability and Stage3 chain has concrete depth diagnostics/directions (4). Controls/failure criterion are discussed but not fully specified as three matched arms (3). It can be implemented with listed operations and safeguards, but parent-conditioned cache/update conventions and inverse transport need precise validation (3). A materially different branch-frame failure mode offers some exploration value, though it remains close to measured successor steering (2).

SCORE: train_cooccur_hyperbolic_capacity | behavior_evidence=3 | geometry_necessity=3 | novelty=3 | downstream_mechanism=4 | falsifiability=3 | implementability=2 | exploration_value=3
SCOPE: train_cooccur_hyperbolic_capacity | OUT_OF_SCOPE | It explicitly couples train-only co-consumption affinity, hyperbolic cost, Sinkhorn parent assignment, and curved residual transport. The proposal does not explicitly name behavior-off, Euclidean geometry-off, and both-on comparison arms; its general “both ablations” statement is underspecified. Specify all three matched comparisons.
EVIDENCE: train_cooccur_hyperbolic_capacity | 6e1c1bef369ac4ea:E1 6e1c1bef369ac4ea:E2 6e1c1bef369ac4ea:E5 6e1c1bef369ac4ea:E9 6e1c1bef369ac4ea:E12 6e1c1bef369ac4ea:E13 6e1c1bef369ac4ea:E14 6e1c1bef369ac4ea:E15 6e1c1bef369ac4ea:E16
OBJECTION: train_cooccur_hyperbolic_capacity | The specified dense B² batch-affinity term is expensive at B≈1,023, while sparse-top-neighbor/block approximation changes the assignment calculation and its cost is not reconciled with the claimed frozen budget.
COUNTEREXAMPLE: train_cooccur_hyperbolic_capacity | If a minibatch has no cached co-consumption edges (or lambda=0), the affinity tilt vanishes and the Sinkhorn-plus-curved assignment is not behavior-coupled; Sinkhorn capacity alone cannot establish the claimed coupling.
RATIONALE: train_cooccur_hyperbolic_capacity | E2 specifies the train-only signal, but the cited measured evidence (E9) is predecessor-profile overlap rather than within-window co-consumption affinity, so support is plausible but indirect (3; bounded check: measure PMI-neighbor positive/negative lift and coverage). The curved cost/transport are explicit (E12-E14), but matched Euclidean Sinkhorn can reproduce much of the transform and necessity is not shown (3). Batch affinity plus entropic transport is distinct from itemwise successor scoring; cited work/ledger trace is absent (3; bounded check: compare exact computation to ledger). Soft-parent context → later assignments → prefix survival and Stage3 metrics is articulated (4). The failure condition and diagnostics are present, but comparisons are not fully defined/matched (3). As written it is implementable in principle, but dense cost and the projected weighted ball mean/row-column mass conventions require resolving before frozen-budget implementation (2). It explores a batch-level assignment failure mode with an informative resource/affinity tradeoff (3).

SCORE: successor-chart-residual | behavior_evidence=4 | geometry_necessity=3 | novelty=2 | downstream_mechanism=4 | falsifiability=3 | implementability=2 | exploration_value=2
SCOPE: successor-chart-residual | OUT_OF_SCOPE | It names a train-only directed successor distribution and uses its hyperbolic barycenter to define the chart for curved T2/T3 residual quantization, changing the assignment. However, it does not explicitly specify behavior-off, Euclidean geometry-off, and both-on comparisons; references to “both ablations” do not define these arms. Add that matched comparison set.
EVIDENCE: successor-chart-residual | b2bc7b945748e74c:E1 b2bc7b945748e74c:E2 b2bc7b945748e74c:E5 b2bc7b945748e74c:E12 b2bc7b945748e74c:E13 b2bc7b945748e74c:E14 b2bc7b945748e74c:E15 b2bc7b945748e74c:E16
OBJECTION: successor-chart-residual | The chart barycenter is computed from successor embeddings but the specification does not establish that those embeddings are aligned to continuation modes relevant to the current residual; the chart may shift coordinates without making children more predictive.
COUNTEREXAMPLE: successor-chart-residual | For a single successor, b_i equals that successor point (up to smoothing); if the current residual and all codewords are shifted by the same chart isometry and inverse transport is exact, pairwise distances and nearest-code assignments are unchanged, yielding no benefit from charting.
RATIONALE: successor-chart-residual | E5 supports nonuniform successor entropy and E10 reports transition coverage, but does not measure chart usefulness for residuals (4; bounded check: evaluate residual-neighbor concentration by successor-profile strata). Geodesic chart operations are explicit (E12-E14), yet a chart change can be equivalent to a matched Euclidean coordinate transform and no curvature-specific advantage/cancellation analysis is supplied (3). Difference from cited work/ledger is asserted computationally, but traceable sources are not provided (2; bounded check: equation-level comparison against ledger). The assignment-to-token predictability-to-beam chain and diagnostics are stated (4). The controls are referenced but not specified with a failure criterion in matched detail (3). Implementability is impaired by the assignment equation appearing to apply exp_b to v=log_b(r), which recovers r, and by ambiguous subtraction/inverse-chart conventions (2; bounded check: unit-test chart round trip and tensor dimensions). A local-chart alternative is somewhat distinct but close to measured successor geodesic/tangent residual families (2).

SCORE: branching-curvature-budget | behavior_evidence=4 | geometry_necessity=3 | novelty=2 | downstream_mechanism=4 | falsifiability=3 | implementability=2 | exploration_value=2
SCOPE: branching-curvature-budget | OUT_OF_SCOPE | It directly conditions per-item negative curvature on train-only successor branching and uses that curvature in residual assignment and a transition regularizer, satisfying computational coupling. But behavior-off, Euclidean geometry-off, and both-on comparisons are not explicitly specified as matched arms; the generic “each ablation” language is insufficient. Define those comparisons.
EVIDENCE: branching-curvature-budget | 1acdc4472893a05c:E1 1acdc4472893a05c:E2 1acdc4472893a05c:E5 1acdc4472893a05c:E12 1acdc4472893a05c:E13 1acdc4472893a05c:E14 1acdc4472893a05c:E15 1acdc4472893a05c:E16
OBJECTION: branching-curvature-budget | Per-item curvature changes the metric scale based on entropy, but the proposal does not show that normalized branching—not count/support or popularity—should determine curvature, and combines this with multiple regularizers that make the source of any effect hard to identify.
COUNTEREXAMPLE: branching-curvature-budget | If all items have h_i=1, then c_i=c_min for all items: the behavior-conditioned curvature becomes a single global curvature and no longer allocates curvature by branching, although the curved quantizer remains.
RATIONALE: branching-curvature-budget | E5 gives auditable entropy/top-1 stratification, though it does not establish that entropy should control geometric curvature (4). Hyperbolic distance at item-conditioned curvature is explicit (E12-E14), but curvature scaling could be matched by Euclidean rescaling and no necessity/cancellation argument is given (3). The idea is distinct in form but lies within routine behavior-conditioned geometry and has no traceable prior-art/ledger comparison (2; bounded check: compare full per-item metric equation with cited work and ledger). Its proposed hierarchy → branching allocation → beam survival chain has named diagnostics and directions (4). Ablations/failure criterion are mentioned but not specified as matched controls (3). Curvature scaling and sparse regularization are plausible, but the tail-balance entropy expression and discrete successor-code lookup/neighbor update need exact definitions and numerical testing (2). The mechanism is a variation on measured successor-entropy/geodesic families (2).
EOF
